title: Secure File Uploads
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of secure file uploads and at least two listed subtopics.

content.intro: Learn secure file uploads through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Secure File Uploads matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines secure file uploads as part of static files, media, and file storage. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: File size limits; Content and extension validation; Untrusted file names; Isolating user uploads; Safe serving and download permissions. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.text: Model permissions are a useful starting point but do not automatically enforce ownership of every individual record. Scope each lookup and mutation to the caller’s authorized objects.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Secure File Uploads
content_blocks.expected_output: The helper rejects filenames with unapproved suffixes as one narrow validation layer.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open a local project using the documented Django 6.1-compatible Python environment. If this snippet depends on model names, URL configuration, settings, or an optional package, add those prerequisites before running it. Otherwise inspect it as a static example. CodeLeaf browser preview does not execute Django/Python server code.
content_blocks.troubleshooting: A filename suffix is not proof of safe content. Enforce size limits, inspect content where appropriate, store outside executable paths, and control private-file access.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
